title: Cabin Window Frame Corner — Crack Repair by Bolted Doubler

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Window Frame Structure

abstract: Permanent repair for cracking at the corner of a cabin window frame, using a bolted doubler on the internal face that carries the hoop load around the crack without disturbing the window itself.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the hoop load path around a cracked cabin window frame corner and allows the aircraft to continue in service without replacing the frame.
sections.damage_assessment: Remove the cabin lining locally and find the crack tip by eddy current inspection; the crack is normally longer than it appears because it runs under the frame flange. Cracks up to 25 mm measured from the corner radius tangent, in one corner only of a given window, and not extending into the skin panel, are inside this repair. A crack that has reached the skin panel, a second crack in the same frame, or any crack in a window frame adjacent to an existing repair, is outside it. Inspect the two frames forward and aft of the damaged one before deciding; corner cracking often appears in a run of three windows and repairing one at a time is not economic.
sections.repair_procedure: Stop drill the crack 4 mm beyond the confirmed tip with a 4.0 mm drill and ream the hole. Do an eddy current inspection to confirm the tip is contained. Cut the doubler from the window frame kit D5620124544147 material to the layout of repair drawing RD-56-20-12-008 and drill the fastener pattern using the doubler as a template, working from the internal face only. CAUTION: DO NOT DRILL THROUGH INTO THE SKIN PANEL. THE DRAWING GIVES THE MAXIMUM DRILL DEPTH. Deburr and apply the chromate-free primer to all new surfaces. Where the lower doubler D5620125694014 is already fitted at the same corner, use the alternate layout on sheet 2, which offsets the fastener rows. Install the doubler wet with sealant, fastened with swaged collars AES253143-9B on the two outer rows. Restore the pressure seal and the internal trim. Where the splice plate D5620126099302 lies under the doubler footprint, do not fasten through it; the drawing gives the exclusion zone.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 24 000 flight cycles from embodiment. Do a repeat eddy current inspection of the stop drill hole and of the doubler perimeter every 6 000 flight cycles, with the lining removed. Do a detailed visual inspection of the window frame corner from the cabin at every C-check; a witness mark in the trim usually appears before the eddy current finds growth. Any growth from the stop drill hole invalidates the repair. Report the repair to Aeralis with the window position and the aircraft cycles.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 25 mm from the corner radius tangent, one corner only per window, not extending into the skin panel, and not adjacent to an existing repaired window.

repair_drawings.title: Bolted doubler, cabin window frame corner

materials.description: CLIP KIT, WINDOW FRAME STRUCTURE, UPPER

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of 22 collars AES253143-9B at 19 mm pitch and 13 mm edge distance, staggered, with the exclusion zone on sheet 2 left unfastened
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 24 000 flight cycles; repeat eddy current inspection every 6 000 flight cycles with the lining removed.

issue.reason: The acceptance criterion for the local stiffness step the doubler introduces at the bonded interface is written out, so that it can be cited rather than re-derived.

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Window Frame Structure

abstract: Permanent repair for cracking at the corner of a cabin window frame, using a bolted doubler on the internal face that carries the hoop load around the crack without disturbing the window itself.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the hoop load path around a cracked cabin window frame corner and allows the aircraft to continue in service without replacing the frame. It also records the acceptance criterion used for the local stiffness step the doubler introduces at the bonded interface, which is generic to the transparency surround and not specific to this repair.
sections.damage_assessment: Remove the cabin lining locally and find the crack tip by eddy current inspection; the crack is normally longer than it appears because it runs under the frame flange. Cracks up to 25 mm measured from the corner radius tangent, in one corner only of a given window, and not extending into the skin panel, are inside this repair. A crack that has reached the skin panel, a second crack in the same frame, or any crack in a window frame adjacent to an existing repair, is outside it. Inspect the two frames forward and aft of the damaged one before deciding; corner cracking often appears in a run of three windows and repairing one at a time is not economic.
sections.repair_procedure: Stop drill the crack 4 mm beyond the confirmed tip with a 4.0 mm drill and ream the hole. Do an eddy current inspection to confirm the tip is contained. Cut the doubler from the window frame kit D5620124544147 material to the layout of repair drawing RD-56-20-12-008 and drill the fastener pattern using the doubler as a template, working from the internal face only. CAUTION: DO NOT DRILL THROUGH INTO THE SKIN PANEL. THE DRAWING GIVES THE MAXIMUM DRILL DEPTH. Deburr and apply the chromate-free primer to all new surfaces. Where the lower doubler D5620125694014 is already fitted at the same corner, use the alternate layout on sheet 2, which offsets the fastener rows. Install the doubler wet with sealant, fastened with swaged collars AES253143-9B on the two outer rows. Restore the pressure seal and the internal trim. Where the splice plate D5620126099302 lies under the doubler footprint, do not fasten through it; the drawing gives the exclusion zone. The doubler run-out is tapered over the last 40 mm for a reason: the acceptance for a bonded interface of this kind is that the in-plane stiffness step at the edge of the added material stays below fifteen per cent of the parent, measured over 40 mm, which is what keeps the peel stress at the adhesive fillet inside the allowable. The taper on the drawing achieves eleven per cent. Any departure from the drawn run-out has to be shown to meet the same figure.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 24 000 flight cycles from embodiment. Do a repeat eddy current inspection of the stop drill hole and of the doubler perimeter every 6 000 flight cycles, with the lining removed. Do a detailed visual inspection of the window frame corner from the cabin at every C-check; a witness mark in the trim usually appears before the eddy current finds growth. Inspect the doubler run-out edge at the same time: a lifted fillet at the tapered end is the first sign that the stiffness step is not being carried as designed. Any growth from the stop drill hole invalidates the repair. Report the repair to Aeralis with the window position and the aircraft cycles.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 25 mm from the corner radius tangent, one corner only per window, not extending into the skin panel, and not adjacent to an existing repaired window.
